description: Bronze Age Hillfort, primarily occupied through the middle - late iron age. A rectangular structure in the central plateau beginning to the Late Iron age - Early Roman phase was interpreted as a shrine. There appears to be destruction during the Roman invasion, followed by a phase where it's  occupied by the Roman military, and subsequently abandoned at the end of 1st CE. Re-occupation in the later 5th CE and beyond.
bibliography: Barrett, Freeman, and Woodward. “Cadbury Castle, Somerset. The Late Prehistoric and Early Historic Archaeology.” English Heritage Archaeological Monograph 20 (2000). http://dx.doi.org/10.5284/1028203.
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Cadbury Castle (South Cadbury).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
